solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Show no respect employing bodies for strip

indicators.note: to employ something is to take it on, so the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: to diss someone is to disrespect them
posses are bodies of men gathered by a sheriff

explanation.surface: Someone is being rude by using bodies to strip, as if in a lurid scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of their property is to deprive them of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Silky hair to the ground

definitions.meaning: fine soft feathers or hair, as on a chick
downward, towards the floor, as in fall over

explanation.surface: Long silky hair reaching right to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is fluffy fine plumage; the other is the adverb for lower or groundward.

clue.text: Chassis of lorry almost tons with solid exterior

indicators.note: the word for solid forms the outside, wrapping the rest

parts.note: sure can mean solid or reliable, as in a sure footing

indicators.note: the word for lorry is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a truck is a lorry

explanation.surface: A truck's chassis, almost tons in weight, with a solid outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the frame of a vehicle, a framework or build.

clue.text: Look up and study antique

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an archaic word for look
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Examining and researching an antique item.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden means of long ago, ancient or antique.

clue.text: Cushions regularly needed on board ship

indicators.note: being on board means being within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
often means frequently, regularly

explanation.surface: Cushions that are frequently needed aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion a blow is to soften it, so the verb form matches.

clue.text: Sneak before church avoiding a crush

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second
the word avoids the letter, so it is taken out

parts.note: to squeal is to inform or sneak on someone

explanation.surface: A telltale, before going to church, avoids a squeeze in the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To squelch something is to crush or suppress it.

clue.text: Kills aristocrats? Not at first

indicators.note: the word for aristocrats loses its opening letter, being 'not' there at the start

parts.note: toffs is British slang for upper-class people

explanation.surface: A question hinting at revolutionaries executing the nobility, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFFS is British slang for posh, upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb: to off someone is to murder them, so the third-person form matches.

clue.text: Stone following dressing

parts.note: lint is a fabric used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: A stone found after a bandage, as though removed from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint is a hard grey kind of rock or stone.

clue.text: Bit eaten up in tortano, it's egg usually

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards
the letters are consumed within these words

explanation.surface: A morsel eaten in a tortano, a stuffed Italian bread usually made with egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit, as in a hint or trace of something, is a synonym.

clue.text: Far-out to have insiders cycling on drugs

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word rotate, the first of them moving to the back of the inner group

parts.note: far-out means weird, strange

explanation.surface: Something bizarre whose insides are spinning, as if high on narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insiders cycling' turns the inner letters EIR of WEIRD into IRE, leaving W and D in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang usage: being wired means being high or hyped up on stimulants.

clue.text: Outcast Foreign Office flunkey's no ruler

indicators.note: the flunkey has no ruler, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a flunkey is a servile underling; the 's reads as 'has'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen or ruler

explanation.surface: A disgraced civil-service lackey with no monarch to serve has been cast out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of flunkey's means 'has'; 'no' removes ER (Elizabeth Regina, the Queen) from UNDERLING, giving UNDLING.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned infant is a foundling, an outcast child left by its parents.

clue.text: Composer of the French swallows rising spleen

indicators.note: the French word swallows the reversed one

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards

parts.note: bile and spleen both mean bad temper

explanation.surface: A French composer swallowing his rising anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Delibes was a French composer, of the ballet Coppelia.

clue.text: Get hard criminal offender back taking Ecstasy

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: the reversed word takes in the drug's letter
the word for offender is written backwards

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual offender
E is the common abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tough villain returns to prison and starts taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG reversed by 'back' gives GAL, which 'taking' wraps around E to make GEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquids that set or solidify are said to congeal, becoming hard or firm.

clue.text: Drink tea, it's said, in previous container

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for previous
the word for previous acts as the vessel holding the other letter

parts.note: late can mean former or previous, as in the late president

indicators.note: signals the word tea is spoken, sounding like a letter of the alphabet

parts.note: spoken, tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A beverage of tea served in an old cup, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is a milky coffee, a kind of drink ordered in cafes.

clue.text: See son wearing majestic old crown

indicators.note: the letter is worn inside the word for majestic

parts.note: epic means grand, majestic
the pate is the crown of the head

explanation.surface: A son in regal old crown, like a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his diocese, the office of a bishop.

clue.text: Such as snips and snails and puppy-dogs' tails?

definitions.text: Such as snips and snails and puppy-dogs' tails?

parts.words: Such as snips and snails and puppy-dogs' tails?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme line about what little boys are made of lists nouns that all end in S, each in its multiple form

explanation.surface: Quotes the nursery rhyme saying what little boys are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Every noun in the list is in its many-items grammatical form, so they are examples of that category.

clue.text: A mid-evening nap keeps the old getting upset

parts.note: the middle letter of the word evening

indicators.note: the word for nap holds the old word

parts.note: nod, as in nodding off, is a short sleep
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A doze in the evening keeps the elderly from being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed means irritated or upset, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Tile possibly covers a small home

indicators.note: the headgear sits over and around the other letters

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat, hence the 'possibly'
a small amount is a bit, so a small gives these letters

explanation.surface: A roof tile covering a small house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home or environment of an animal or plant.

clue.text: Thrill seeing one work in gallery

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
I is the Roman numeral for one
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Seeing a single work of art in a gallery is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries, best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse, so thrill fits as a verb.

clue.text: Bone in back's reportedly senseless

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship; the 's reads as 'is'

indicators.note: the word for senseless is heard rather than seen, its final B being silent

parts.note: numb means without feeling, senseless

explanation.surface: A bone in the back is said to have lost all feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'stern numb' runs its two N sounds together and the B is silent, so 'reportedly' leaves only UM to follow STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone in the chest is a bone known anatomically by this name.

clue.text: Regretted being cut holding vase for wife

indicators.note: one item stands in for the other, the vase replacing the wife

parts.note: mowed means cut, as of grass
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A mourning widower who has been hurt, holding an urn instead of his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mourned is to have grieved or regretted something.

clue.text: Dish remains lavish in Italian capital, half cut

indicators.note: the letters go inside the trimmed city name
only the first half of the city's name is kept

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
is can mean remains or exists, as in 'is still'
OTT, over the top, means excessive or lavish

explanation.surface: A meal in Rome is lavish yet cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT means over the top; 'half cut' keeps the first half of ROME, and 'in' places the other pieces between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Circle both hands, cupping over and beneath cut

indicators.note: the pair hold the other letters between them

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left
O is the abbreviation for over in cricket

indicators.note: the word for beneath loses its last letter

parts.note: under means beneath

explanation.surface: Holding a circle with both hands, cupping over and below the wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a small disc or circle, such as the RAF marking.

clue.text: Strangely religious, not starting to accept God

indicators.note: the shortened word takes in a letter
the word for religious loses its opening letter

parts.note: godly means devout, religious
D is an abbreviation for God, from Latin Deus

explanation.surface: A devout person behaving strangely by refusing to begin by accepting God.
explanation.walkthrough: D for God (Latin Deus) is placed in ODLY, which is GODLY with 'not starting' removing G.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb for in a peculiar or curious way is a direct synonym of strangely.

clue.text: Even new district's on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the up means read upwards

parts.note: a ward is an electoral district

explanation.surface: A newly developed district is doing better.
explanation.definitionFit: A match that ended level is drawn, so the score is even.

clue.text: Bizarre burn-out's curable now and then

indicators.note: taking a letter only now and then picks out every other one

explanation.surface: A strange case of exhaustion that can be cured only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bizarre is out of the ordinary, a synonym of strange or rare.

clue.text: Amateur gesture suppresses desires

indicators.note: the two words keep the letters held down within them

explanation.surface: A novice's gesture keeps down their longings.
explanation.definitionFit: Urges are strong desires or impulses.

clue.text: Advanced producing fast time

definitions.meaning: the forty-day Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Something moved forward produces a quick time.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past tense of loan; the other is the season of fasting before Easter.

clue.text: Ace team playing with England's outside left

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a band is a group or team of people
on means playing, as in a show being on
the outer letters of the word England, its first and last

explanation.surface: A star sports team playing with England's outside-left winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in the sense of deserted or forsaken, the past participle of a verb meaning to desert.

clue.text: Crop that's good to destroy

parts.note: to raze is to demolish or destroy

explanation.surface: A harvest that is good to wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals crop grass by grazing it, eating the tips of the pasture.

clue.text: Bird trapped in tavern escaped

indicators.note: the bird's letters are held within the run of these two words

explanation.surface: A bird caught in a pub got away.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword staple bird.

clue.text: Youthful adult practically elderly in decline

parts.note: A is the old film certificate for adult viewing

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the word for decline

parts.note: a descent is a decline or fall

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: old means elderly

explanation.surface: A grown-up, nearly old, is going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practically' trims OLD to OL, which goes into DESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, it describes someone in their teens, hence youthful.
